claims.text: What the strip looks like A narrow QRS at 40–60 (junctional escape) or 60–100 (accelerated), with inverted or absent P waves, or P waves buried in the QRS.
claims.quote: Narrow QRS, rate 40–60 (junctional escape) or 60–100 (accelerated) Inverted or absent P waves, or P buried in QRS

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Rate by name: junctional bradycardia < 40; escape rhythm 40–60; accelerated rhythm 60–100; junctional tachycardia > 100
claims.quote: Junctional bradycardia: < 40 bpm Junctional Escape Rhythm: 40-60 bpm Accelerated Junctional Rhythm: 60-100 bpm Junctional Tachycardia: > 100 bpm
QRS complexes are typically narrow (< 120 ms)
claims.locator: ECG features of Junctional Escape Rhythm

claims.text: P waves: retrograde P waves may come before, during or after the QRS — usually inverted in II, III, aVF and upright in aVR and V1
claims.quote: Retrograde P waves may be present and can appear before, during or after the QRS complex. They are usually inverted in inferior leads (II, III, aVF), upright in aVR + V1

claims.text: Escape rhythm: no relationship between the QRS complexes and any preceding atrial activity (P waves, flutter or fibrillatory waves)
claims.quote: No relationship between the QRS complexes and any preceding atrial activity (e.g. P-waves, flutter waves, fibrillatory waves)
claims.locator: ECG features of Junctional Escape Rhythm

claims.text: Accelerated rhythm: AV dissociation may be present, with the ventricular rate usually above the atrial rate; look for features of digoxin effect or toxicity
claims.quote: AV dissociation may be present with the ventricular rate usually greater than the atrial rate There may be associated ECG features of digoxin effect or digoxin toxicity

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Escape mechanism: a lower pacemaker takes over when the supraventricular impulses reaching the AV node are slower than its own intrinsic rate
claims.quote: Junctional and ventricular escape rhythms arise when the rate of supraventricular impulses arriving at the AV node or ventricle is less than the intrinsic rate of the ectopic pacemaker.

claims.text: Escape causes: severe sinus bradycardia, sinus arrest, sinoatrial exit block, high-grade second-degree or third-degree AV block, hyperkalemia, beta-blocker, calcium-channel-blocker or digoxin poisoning
claims.quote: Severe sinus bradycardia Sinus arrest Sino-atrial exit block High-grade second degree AV block Third degree AV block Hyperkalaemia Drugs: beta-blocker, calcium-channel blocker or digoxin poisoning

claims.text: Accelerated mechanism: increased automaticity in the AV node coupled with decreased automaticity in the sinus node
claims.quote: This situation arises when there is increased automaticity in the AV node coupled with decreased automaticity in the sinus node.

claims.text: Accelerated causes: digoxin toxicity (the classic cause), beta-agonists (isoprenaline, adrenaline), myocardial ischemia, myocarditis, cardiac surgery
claims.quote: Digoxin toxicity (= the classic cause of AJR) Beta-agonists, e.g. isoprenaline, adrenaline Myocardial ischaemia Myocarditis Cardiac surgery

claims.text: Symptoms Accelerated (nonparoxysmal) junctional tachycardia: rate 60–120, so symptoms are usually absent
claims.quote: Heart rate is 60 to 120 beats/minute; thus, symptoms are usually absent.

claims.text: Treatment Accelerated (nonparoxysmal) junctional tachycardia: treat the underlying heart disorder
claims.quote: Treatment is directed at the underlying heart disorder.
